questions.stem: Which organisation initiated the term AIOps, and in which year?
questions.explanation: AIOps was initiated by Gartner in 2016.

questions.stem: AIOps is described as supporting which group of operational disciplines together?
options: DevOps, DataOps, MLOps, DLOps and ITOps
questions.explanation: AIOps supports DevOps, DataOps, MLOps, DLOps and ITOps together, assisting them to work seamlessly.

questions.stem: After which era did AIOps come to the surface, when every kind of operational task had tripled?
questions.explanation: AIOps came to the surface after the inception of the Big Data era, when huge data started to flow in and operational tasks of every kind had tripled.

questions.stem: What key difference separates AIOps from DevOps, MLOps and ITOps?
options: AIOps applies only to on-premises infrastructure
AIOps requires more human interaction than the others
AIOps is limited to data warehousing
AIOps makes sure everything runs on its own, whereas the others still require human interaction
AIOps was introduced before the others
questions.explanation: Unlike DevOps, MLOps and ITOps, where human interactions are still required, AIOps makes sure everything runs on its own.

questions.stem: AIOps uses algorithms to achieve which of the following outcomes?
options: Preventing outages, maintaining uptime and assuring continuous services
questions.explanation: AIOps uses algorithms to make things happen like preventing outages, maintaining uptime and assuring continuous services.

questions.stem: What is the FIRST stage in the end-to-end AIOps operational cycle?
questions.explanation: AIOps first collects data, then removes duplications, relates data with events, enriches the process, minimises, detects, observes and predicts issues, and self-learns before restarting the cycle.

questions.stem: In the AIOps cycle, what does the system do in the final stage before restarting all the stages again?
questions.explanation: The last stage of the AIOps cycle is to self-learn and then restart all the stages again.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the stages of the AIOps operational cycle?
options: Relate data with events in the cycle of operations
Manually escalate issues to a human operator
questions.explanation: AIOps handles end-to-end operations on its own; manual escalation to a human operator is not one of its stages.

questions.stem: AIOps came into the picture partly because organisations were progressing in data while ignoring what requirement of automation?
questions.explanation: Everyone wanted to progress in data, ignoring the fact that automation requires processes and governance; that is why AIOps came into the picture, where everything is handled by the system itself.

questions.stem: In the AIOps cycle, which stage sits immediately after issues are detected and observed?
questions.explanation: The AIOps stages run: collect data, remove duplications, relate data with events, enrich the process, minimise issues, detect issues, observe issues, predict issues, then self-learn and restart.
